info.name: B2C Admin API (phase 1)
info.description:
Every endpoint that exists in the code today — 68 operations across `/api/v1/public/*`, `/api/v1/admin/*` and the three un-enveloped file routes.

**Scope.** `docs/API.md` specifies roughly 150 operations; this collection carries only the ones phase 1 actually implements. Deliberately absent, because they answer 404 today: the whole `/api/v1/webhooks/*` tree (no routes registered), the five product verticals, the rest of §26 (`places/`, `stations/`, `airlines/`, `currencies/`), orders, payments, promo codes, content, leads, reports, notification templates, `settings/menu/`, `profile/cards/`, `profile/notifications/`, `integrations/gts/test/`, `integrations/payments/{code}/test/` and `auth/devices/`. `docs/API.md` remains the full contract.

**Before you start.** Run the stack (`docker compose up -d`, or `uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000`), then open the collection's *Variables* tab and set `origin` if you are not on `http://localhost:8000`.

**Tokens are automatic.** `Admin ▸ Auth ▸ login` writes `adminAccessToken`/`adminRefreshToken`; `Public ▸ Auth ▸ login` (and `register/confirm`, `social`, `refresh`) writes `accessToken`/`refreshToken`. Folders inherit the right bearer token, so nothing has to be pasted by hand.

**Three things that bite.**
1. Every path ends in a slash. The app runs with `redirect_slashes=False`, so dropping it is a hard 404, never a redirect.
2. The login body field is `login`, not `email` — on both surfaces.
3. The auth folders are rate limited to 5 requests per minute per IP, enforced in Redis and surviving a restart. A 429 carries `Retry-After`.

**Envelope.** Every `/api/v1/*` response is `{status, data, errors, meta}`. List endpoints put the rows in `data` and `{page, page_size, total, total_pages}` in `meta`. The `/healthz` and `/uploads/*` routes are outside it.

**Audiences.** A customer token on `/admin/*` is a **403**, not a 401 — the token is valid, it is just for the other surface.

variable.description: Scheme and host only. The app declares no host/port itself — this is whatever uvicorn or docker-compose published.
The API root. The `/api/v1` prefix is hard-coded in app/api/v1/router.py.
FIRST_OWNER_EMAIL from .env — the account docker/bootstrap.py creates on first boot.
Customer access token (aud: public), 30 min. Written by the Public ▸ Auth scripts.
Customer refresh token, 30 days, rotated on every refresh.
Staff access token (aud: admin), 15 min. Written by the Admin ▸ Auth scripts.
Staff refresh token, 12 hours, rotated on every refresh.
The 4-digit code from the email. A string, because leading zeros are part of it.
Written by Public ▸ Auth ▸ password/reset/verify. Single use, 15 min.
The storage key inside an upload's `url` — the tail after /uploads/.

item.name: Public
item.description: `/api/v1/public/*` — the website and the Flutter app. Subject `aud: public`. Rate limited to 120 requests per minute, except the auth folder which is far tighter.

item.name: Site config
item.description: API.md §17. The first call a cold client makes, and the only one it cannot start without.

header.description: Paste the ETag from a previous response to get a 304 with no body.

query.description: uz | ru | en. Beats Accept-Language. The response echoes the language actually served in `data.lang`.

request.description:
Branding, languages, currencies, products, enabled payment methods, menu and feature flags in one document.

No auth. Answers with `ETag` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`; the cache is dropped by any settings write, which is what makes a colour change visible without a deploy.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
API.md §18. **Rate limited to 5 requests per minute per IP** — the limit lives on the router, so registration and resend share it with login. A 429 carries `Retry-After`.

OTP rules: 4 digits, 10-minute TTL, 5 wrong attempts burn the code, a new code instantly burns the previous one, and resend is silently throttled to one per 60 seconds.

Local SMTP swallows the mail — read the code out of the application log.

request.description:
Only `email` and `password` are required; `first_name`, `last_name` and `phone` are optional and may be omitted entirely.

**Always 204**, even when the address is already taken — otherwise this endpoint would tell an anonymous caller who has an account here. Sends the 4-digit code by email.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
console.log('customer tokens saved, access expires in ' + body.data.expires_in + 's');
console.log('no tokens saved (HTTP ' + pm.response.code + ') — existing ones left alone');

request.description:
Exchanges the emailed code for an access + refresh pair, and confirms the account.

`code` is a **string** of exactly 4 characters. Set `otpCode` in the collection variables first.
204 either way. The 60-second gap between codes is enforced silently — a call inside it still answers 204 and simply sends nothing.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
console.log('customer tokens saved, access expires in ' + body.data.expires_in + 's');
console.log('no tokens saved (HTTP ' + pm.response.code + ') — existing ones left alone');

request.description:
The field is **`login`**, not `email` — though in this release it is validated as an email address; phone + SMS comes later.

Returns `{access_token, refresh_token, expires_in}`, where `expires_in` describes the **access** token in seconds. The test script stores both tokens.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
console.log('no rotation (HTTP ' + pm.response.code + ') — existing tokens left alone');

request.description:
Rotation, not renewal: the old refresh token is revoked as the new pair is issued.

Replaying an already-revoked refresh token is read as theft and **kills every session of that customer**. So do not run this twice from the same stored value.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
console.log('customer tokens saved via social sign-in');

request.description:
`google` is the only provider this release resolves. Any other name — and a provider switched off in the panel — is a **404**, on purpose: an anonymous caller learns nothing about which providers exist.

`id_token` is the identity token Google handed the browser. Requires `client_id` to be set under Admin ▸ Integrations ▸ Social and the provider enabled.

The one authenticated endpoint in this folder: the caller proves the session is theirs before it ends, so a leaked refresh token is not also a way to sign somebody out.

204.
204 whether or not the address is known. Sends a 4-digit code.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
console.log('reset token saved, valid for ' + body.data.expires_in + 's');

request.description: Exchanges the code for a single-use `reset_token` (15 minutes). The test script stores it as `resetToken`.

The field is **`reset_token`** here. (The admin surface calls the same field `token` — the two are not interchangeable.)

`new_password` is 8–128 characters. 204, and every session of that customer is killed.

item.name: Profile
item.description: API.md §19. The whole folder needs a customer token — the guard sits on the router, not on individual handlers, so a blocked, unconfirmed or deleted account is refused before any handler runs.

request.description:
Returns `id, email, first_name, last_name, middle_name, phone, birth_date, avatar_id, avatar_url, created_at, is_profile_complete`.

No `is_blocked`: a blocked account cannot reach this endpoint at all, so the field could only ever read `false`.

`is_profile_complete` is derived and read-only: `true` only when all five of `first_name`, `last_name`, `middle_name`, `phone` and `birth_date` are filled. Whitespace does not count as filled. Sending it to `PATCH` is a 422.

**These five fields and nothing else.** The model is `extra="forbid"`, so sending `email` or `is_profile_complete` — or any other key — is a 422 naming the field. The address is what the OTP proved and what password reset trusts, so it cannot be changed here.

Partial: only the keys present change.

**A DELETE with a request body.** This is the one irreversible thing a customer token can do, so holding the token is not enough — the password is asked for again.

204. Some HTTP clients drop bodies on DELETE; Postman does not.
204, and **every session is killed** — including the token this request used. Sign in again afterwards.

formdata.description: png, jpeg or webp. Max 1 MB. No SVG — raster only.

request.description:
`multipart/form-data` with a single `file` part — no `purpose` field, unlike `/admin/uploads/`, because on this route it could only ever be `avatar`.

Pick a file in the Body tab before sending. The bytes are magic-sniffed; the `Content-Type` the client claims is not trusted. Returns the updated profile.

Do not set `Content-Type` by hand — Postman writes the multipart boundary itself.

item.name: Passengers
item.description: API.md §19 — saved passengers, the standard CRUD shape. Another customer's passenger is a **404**, not a 403: the caller learns nothing about rows that are not theirs.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring over first_name and last_name.
first_name | last_name | birth_date | created_at, optionally with a leading '-'. Default -created_at. Anything else is a 422 on the `ordering` field.
Inclusive. A datetime sent without an offset is read as UTC.

request.description: Paginated: rows in `data`, `{page, page_size, total, total_pages}` in `meta`.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }

request.description:
`first_name`, `last_name` and `birth_date` are required; `middle_name`, `citizenship` and the document fields are optional. A passenger without a birth date would still have to be retyped before it could be booked, so it is refused here rather than at booking. `document_type` (max 32) and `citizenship` (max 64) are free text — the catalogues of document types and countries are GTS's and have no endpoint yet, and a country code would also mean choosing a standard the contract has not named.

201. The test script stores the new id as `passengerId`.
`id` is a UUID; a malformed one is a 422, a valid one belonging to somebody else is a 404.

Partial, and `extra="forbid"` — an unknown key is a 422. Settable: `first_name`, `last_name`, `middle_name`, `birth_date`, `citizenship`, `document_type`, `document_number`, `document_expiry_date`.

Sending `null` for `first_name`, `last_name` or `birth_date` is a 422 naming the field — those three have no NULL in the table. The optional fields may be cleared with `null`; that is the only way to remove a stored document number.

item.name: Catalog
item.description:
API.md §26 — the lists a passenger form is filled in from, plus airport autocomplete for the flight search form. **No auth**, and none is possible: the form is rendered before there is anything to authenticate.

All three are a passthrough to GTS's `/static/*` service, which needs no account of its own, so they work on an installation that has not yet saved a GTS credential. Items arrive in **GTS's own shape**: the `translations` object is kept whole and no `lang` is added, which is the one exemption from API.md §7.

For `document-types/` and `countries/` the answer is held in Redis for 24 hours and carries `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`. The first call takes as long as GTS does (~0.4 s); every one after it is served locally. `airports/` is **uncached** — a free-text `q` would make an unbounded cache key — so every search reaches GTS live. A GTS failure is a 502 with its original code in `meta.upstream`, a timeout a 504 — and neither is cached.

query.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, exactly two letters — anything else is a 422. Adds the documents only that country issues; omit it for the universal set. Each value is cached under its own key.

request.description: Passenger document types. `data[].type` is the code to store in `passengers.document_type` (`PSP`, `ZC`, `NP`, `SR`, `DP`, `SPU`, `VV`); `data[].translations` carries the label per language.
216 countries. `data[].code` is the alpha-2 code, alongside `phone_code`, `phone_mask`, `emoji` and a flag image URL — enough for both the citizenship field and a phone input.

query.description: Optional. Airport name, city or IATA code fragment — 2 to 64 characters when present, anything else is a 422. Free text: spaces and non-Latin scripts are fine. Omit the parameter entirely to get GTS's complete airport list.

request.description: Airport autocomplete for the flight search form. A live proxy to GTS `/static/airports/{q}` — **never cached**, every keystroke's request reaches GTS.

item.name: Flight
item.description:
API.md §20 — the search flow, a **live passthrough** to GTS `/v1/content/*` through the installation's active credential. Request and response shapes are GTS's own, verbatim: the body is forwarded after a light shape check, and GTS's `data` comes back untouched inside our envelope.

Auth is **optional** — anonymous searches are welcome; a presented but invalid token is still a 401. Rate limited to 30 requests per minute (the `search` bucket) on top of the public 120.

Gated by `product_settings`, not a feature flag: a vertical the installation does not sell answers 404. No active GTS credential → 502. Nothing is stored on our side (D2): GTS keeps the only cache, keyed by `request_id`.

request.description: Starts a search; GTS answers immediately with `data.request_id` (an opaque string — keep it verbatim for `offers/`). Providers keep answering in the background. Extra GTS fields (`flexible`, `airlines`, `passengers_ids`, …) pass through as sent.

Pages through the offers of a search. Cursor pagination via `next_token` (`null` on the first page); keep polling while results are still arriving. `data` — `offers[]`, `count`, `trip_type`, `next_token` — is GTS's shape, untouched.

item.name: Admin
item.description:
`/api/v1/admin/*` — the React panel. Subject `aud: admin`, rate limited to 300 requests per minute per staff member.

Two roles only, `owner ⊃ admin`. Requests marked **[owner]** answer 403 to an `admin` token. A *customer* token anywhere in this tree is also a 403 — the token is valid, it is just for the other surface.

Both principals are re-read from the database on every request, so blocking or deleting somebody takes effect immediately.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
API.md §27. **Rate limited to 5 requests per minute per IP.**

Admin tokens are short: access 15 minutes, refresh 12 hours.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
console.log('staff tokens saved, access expires in ' + body.data.expires_in + 's');
console.log('no tokens saved (HTTP ' + pm.response.code + ') — existing ones left alone');

request.description:
**Start here.** The field is `login`, not `email`.

The defaults are `FIRST_OWNER_EMAIL` / `FIRST_OWNER_PASSWORD` from `.env` — the owner account `docker/bootstrap.py` creates on first boot. The test script stores the pair as `adminAccessToken` / `adminRefreshToken`, which every other Admin folder uses.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
console.log('no rotation (HTTP ' + pm.response.code + ') — existing tokens left alone');

request.description: Rotating: the old refresh token is revoked. Replaying a revoked one is treated as theft and kills every session of that staff member.
`{id, name, email, role}`. The panel builds its menu from `role`, which comes from the database row, not from the JWT claim.
204, and every session of that staff member is killed — including this one. Update `ownerPassword` afterwards.
204 whether or not the address is known. Emails a reset link — staff get a link, customers get a 4-digit code.

The field is **`token`** here, not `reset_token` — that is the public surface's name for the equivalent field. Paste the value from the emailed link.

204.

item.name: Settings
item.description:
API.md §28. Both roles write here — changing a colour is day-to-day work, not administration of the installation. The one exception is `PATCH features/`.

Every PATCH is partial: a field left out is left alone, so an explicit `null` cannot be used to clear something. Any write here drops the cached `site-config`.

request.description: Colours, font, logo/favicon/app-icon ids, and the resolved `*_url` fields so the panel does not have to build them.

`colors` accepts exactly three keys — `primary`, `accent`, `background` — and each value must be a hex colour (`#RGB` or `#RRGGBB`). Any other key is a 422: the site binds these three to CSS variables, so an extra one would be stored and never rendered.

`font_family` is a closed list: `Inter`, `Roboto`, `Open Sans`, `Montserrat`, `Manrope`. The site ships the faces, so free text would name one the browser cannot load.

`logo_id`, `favicon_id`, `app_icon_id` are UUIDs from Admin ▸ Uploads. `app_name` is max 64 characters.
Name, domain, support contacts, social links. `name` comes back as a translated object.

`name` is translated: keys are language codes. An unsupported code is **silently dropped**, not rejected.

`domain` drives CORS — the middleware resolves the allowed origins per request from this value (`https://<domain>` and `https://www.<domain>` only). Which is why a browser-based client on `http://localhost` will be refused; use Postman or another non-browser client.
`{default, available}`.
This release serves `uz`, `ru`, `en` — anything else is a 422 naming the unsupported codes. `available` must be non-empty; duplicates are removed, order is kept.
`{default, available}`. Defaults to UZS.
Three-letter ISO 4217 codes, upper-cased server-side. `available` must be non-empty.
`{flags: {...}}`. Includes `loyalty`, which is always `false` and cannot be set.

body.raw:
{
  "flags": {
    "blog": true,
    "promotions": true,
    "faq": true,
    "contacts": true,
    "banners": true,
    "popular_directions": true,
    "feedbacks": true,
    "promo_codes": true,
    "leads": true,
    "reports": true,
    "broadcast": true
  }
}

request.description:
**Owner only** — stricter than the rest of this folder, because switching a section off removes it from the client's own site *and* panel.

`flags` is required. The eleven keys above are the complete settable set; `loyalty` is locked and including it is a 422.

A flag set to `false` turns the matching routes into 404 on both surfaces. The data is preserved.

Which verticals are on sale — `[{code, enabled}]`, a bare list with no pagination.

**Read-only by contract:** what an installation may sell follows from its GTS agreement, not from a switch in the panel. There is no PATCH.

Drops the cached `site-config`. **No request body.** 204.

Normally unnecessary — every settings write purges it already.

item.name: Integrations — GTS credentials
item.description:
API.md §29. Reads are open to both roles, writes are **owner only** — the guard is per route, because a router-level `require_owner` would take the reads away from `admin` and a router-level `current_staff` alone would hand `admin` the client's GTS password.

Passwords always come back masked; `CredentialOut` has no field that could carry the real value.

request.description: A bare list, no pagination and no query parameters.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }

request.description:
`label`, `email` and `password` are required; `base_url` defaults to `https://api2.globaltravel.space` and is stored without a trailing slash. A duplicate `label` is a 422.

**The first credential created becomes the active one.** 201; the test script stores the id.
Password masked.
Partial. Sending a `password` replaces it; omitting it keeps the stored one. It cannot be cleared — an account with no password is not a state worth reaching.
Every GTS call from now on uses this account. No request body; returns the credential.
204. Deleting the **active** credential while others exist is a 409 — activate another one first.

item.name: Integrations — SMTP
item.description:
API.md §29. A singleton: no `{id}` and no collection, because an installation sends its mail through one relay.

Transactional mail — OTP codes, password resets — goes through here and is core; it does not hang off the `broadcast` feature flag.

request.description:
`password` is masked when one is stored and `null` when none is — the panel shows those two states differently.

Also returns `last_tested_at`, `last_test_ok`, `last_test_error`.

Partial. `tls` is `starttls`, `ssl` or `none`. `enabled: true` requires `host` and `from_address` to be set — otherwise 422.

`username` and `from_name` are cleared with an **empty string**, not `null`: a relay that needs no authentication is a real configuration, so it has to be reachable from one that did.

Actually sends a message with the stored settings. `to` defaults to the address of whoever pressed the button, so `{}` is a valid body.

Returns the outcome of *trying*, not of the request: a relay that refuses the password answers **200** with `{ok: false, detail, tested_at}`. SMTP switched off or unconfigured is a 409.

This is the only integration probe that works — the GTS and payment provider ones arrive with their adapters in phase 2 and 404 until then.

item.name: Integrations — Payments
item.description:
API.md §29. A registry, not a CRUD resource: every code the release supports has a row whether the client uses it or not, created disabled on first read. There is no POST and no DELETE — adding a provider means shipping an adapter.

`{code}` is `payme` or `click`; anything else is a 422.

request.description: A bare list, credentials masked.
Swap `payme` for `click` in the URL. Returns `{code, enabled, title, logo_id, logo_url, sort_order, credentials, last_tested_at, last_test_ok, last_test_error, created_at, updated_at}`.

**`credentials` merges into what is stored, it does not replace it.** The panel only ever receives them masked, so it could not resend the keys it is not editing. Send `null` as a value to delete that key. At most 20 keys.

A value containing `•` anywhere is treated as a mask and ignored — that is how a masked value read back and sent unchanged does no damage.

Which keys a provider wants comes from that provider's documentation and is **not validated here**; the ones above are illustrative. `enabled: true` requires non-empty credentials. `sort_order` is 0–9999 and decides the order on the site.

item.name: Integrations — Social
item.description:
API.md §29. `{provider}` is `google` only in this release.

`client_id` comes back in full while `client_secret` is masked — not an oversight: the client id is handed to every browser that renders the sign-in button, so hiding it would cost the operator the one value they need to compare against the Google console.

request.description: A bare list of `{provider, enabled, client_id, client_secret, created_at, updated_at}`.

Partial. `enabled: true` requires a `client_id`. An empty string clears a field — the same convention as the SMTP username.

With this off, `POST /public/auth/social/google/` is a 404.

item.name: Staff
item.description:
API.md §38. **The entire resource is owner-only** — `admin` does not appear in the *Jamoa* row of the permission table at all, so it gets a 403 here rather than a filtered view. The guard sits on the router, so no handler can forget it.

Roles are fixed in code: `owner` and `admin`. Anything else is a 422; the panel cannot invent a third.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring over name and email.
name | email | role | created_at | last_login_at, optionally with a leading '-'. Default -created_at.

request.description: Paginated.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }

request.description: All four fields required. `role` is `owner` or `admin`; `password` is 8–128 characters. 201, and the test script stores the id.
Partial: `email`, `name`, `role`. The password is not changed here.
**No request body.** Returns the employee. Takes effect on their very next request — the row is re-read every time, not trusted from the token.
Emails that employee a reset link. **No request body.** 204.

item.name: System
item.description: API.md §39. Read-only, and readable by **both** roles.

request.description: Database, Redis, GTS and payment provider status. Authenticated — for an unauthenticated liveness probe use `GET /healthz` (see the *Un-enveloped* folder).
Backend and panel version. Comes from `APP_VERSION`.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring over actor_email and path.
created_at | resource | action, optionally with a leading '-'. Default -created_at.

request.description:
Who changed what, and when. Paginated.

Append-only: nothing writes here except the audit middleware, so there is no POST and there will not be one. The path sits under `system/` because the contract puts it there, even though the module is `audit`.

item.name: Uploads
item.description:
API.md §11 and §39. A file is uploaded on its own and its `id` is attached to a resource afterwards — which is why this is one endpoint rather than a field on seven others.

Both roles may upload, because both roles edit content. Files that never get attached to anything are swept after 24 hours.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }

formdata.description: The bytes are magic-sniffed; the Content-Type the client claims is not trusted.
logo | favicon | app_icon | blog_cover | promo_banner | banner | document | avatar | payment_logo

request.description:
`multipart/form-data` with `file` and `purpose`. Pick a file in the Body tab before sending.

The purpose decides the allowed MIME types and the size cap: logo and app_icon 2 MB, favicon 1 MB, blog_cover / promo_banner / banner 5 MB, avatar 1 MB (raster only, no SVG), payment_logo 1 MB, document 10 MB. `export` exists as a purpose but cannot be uploaded to.

201 with `{id, url, mime, size}`. The test script stores `uploadId` and derives `uploadKey` from the URL for the file-serving requests.

Do not set `Content-Type` by hand — Postman writes the multipart boundary itself.

item.name: Un-enveloped
item.description:
Outside `/api/v1`, outside the envelope and outside the OpenAPI schema. These serve bytes and a liveness signal, neither of which can be wrapped in `{status, data, errors, meta}`.

Note these use `{{origin}}`, not `{{baseUrl}}`.

request.description:
The container healthcheck. Answers `{"status": "ok"}` with no envelope, no auth and **no trailing slash** — it is deliberately outside the contract, so the API.md slash rule does not apply.

For the real dependency check use `GET /admin/system/health/`.

Serves the bytes behind an upload's `url`. Public — a logo is fetched by anonymous visitors.

`uploadKey` is filled in by the Admin ▸ Uploads script. The key may contain slashes.

The same thing for objects stored private — an export is never fetched anonymously. Requires a staff token.

Private is a property of the stored object, not of the caller: the local storage adapter points private URLs at this route, an S3 adapter would sign them instead.
